# Data Visualization Skill

Chart selection guidance, Python visualization code patterns, design principles, and accessibility considerations for creating effective data visualizations.

## Chart Selection Guide

### Choose by Data Relationship

| What You're Showing | Best Chart | Alternatives |
|---|---|---|
| **Trend over time** | Line chart | Area chart (if showing cumulative or composition) |
| **Comparison across categories** | Vertical bar chart | Horizontal bar (many categories), lollipop chart |
| **Ranking** | Horizontal bar chart | Dot plot, slope chart (comparing two periods) |
| **Part-to-whole composition** | Stacked bar chart | Treemap (hierarchical), waffle chart |
| **Composition over time** | Stacked area chart | 100% stacked bar (for proportion focus) |
| **Distribution** | Histogram | Box plot (comparing groups), violin plot, strip plot |
| **Correlation (2 variables)** | Scatter plot | Bubble chart (add 3rd variable as size) |
| **Correlation (many variables)** | Heatmap (correlation matrix) | Pair plot |
| **Geographic patterns** | Choropleth map | Bubble map, hex map |
| **Flow / process** | Sankey diagram | Funnel chart (sequential stages) |
| **Relationship network** | Network graph | Chord diagram |
| **Performance vs. target** | Bullet chart | Gauge (single KPI only) |
| **Multiple KPIs at once** | Small multiples | Dashboard with separate charts |

### When NOT to Use Certain Charts

- **Pie charts**: Avoid unless <6 categories and exact proportions matter less than rough comparison. Humans are bad at comparing angles. Use bar charts instead.
- **3D charts**: Never. They distort perception and add no information.
- **Dual-axis charts**: Use cautiously. They can mislead by implying correlation. Clearly label both axes if used.
- **Stacked bar (many categories)**: Hard to compare middle segments. Use small multiples or grouped bars instead.
- **Donut charts**: Slightly better than pie charts but same fundamental issues. Use for single KPI display at most.

## Python Visualization Code Patterns

### Setup and Style

```python
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker
import seaborn as sns
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Professional style setup
plt.style.use('seaborn-v0_8-whitegrid')
plt.rcParams.update({
    'figure.figsize': (10, 6),
    'figure.dpi': 150,
    'font.size': 11,
    'axes.titlesize': 14,
    'axes.titleweight': 'bold',
    'axes.labelsize': 11,
    'xtick.labelsize': 10,
    'ytick.labelsize': 10,
    'legend.fontsize': 10,
    'figure.titlesize': 16,
})

# Colorblind-friendly palettes
PALETTE_CATEGORICAL = ['#4C72B0', '#DD8452', '#55A868', '#C44E52', '#8172B3', '#937860']
PALETTE_SEQUENTIAL = 'YlOrRd'
PALETTE_DIVERGING = 'RdBu_r'
```

### Line Chart (Time Series)

```python
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

for label, group in df.groupby('category'):
    ax.plot(group['date'], group['value'], label=label, linewidth=2)

ax.set_title('Metric Trend by Category', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Date')
ax.set_ylabel('Value')
ax.legend(loc='upper left', frameon=True)
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

# Format dates on x-axis
fig.autofmt_xdate()

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('trend_chart.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
```

### Bar Chart (Comparison)

```python
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

# Sort by value for easy reading
df_sorted = df.sort_values('metric', ascending=True)

bars = ax.barh(df_sorted['category'], df_sorted['metric'], color=PALETTE_CATEGORICAL[0])

# Add value labels
for bar in bars:
    width = bar.get_width()
    ax.text(width + 0.5, bar.get_y() + bar.get_height()/2,
            f'{width:,.0f}', ha='left', va='center', fontsize=10)

ax.set_title('Metric by Category (Ranked)', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Metric Value')
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('bar_chart.png', dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
```

### Histogram (Distribution)

```python
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))

ax.hist(df['value'], bins=30, color=PALETTE_CATEGORICAL[0], edgecolor='white', alpha=0.8)

# Add mean and median lines
mean_val = df['value'].mean()
median_val = df['value'].median()
ax.axvline(mean_val, color='red', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5, label=f'Mean: {mean_val:,.1f}')
ax.axvline(median_val, color='green', linestyle='--', linewidth=1.5, label=f'Median: {median_val:,.1f}')

ax.set_title('Distribution of Values', fontweight='bold')
ax.set_xlabel('Value')
ax.set_ylabel('Frequency')
ax.legend()
ax.spines['top'].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['right'].set_visible(False)

# Education Investment vs. Outcomes: 30-Country Comparison

## Overview
This dataset compiles education-related metrics for 30 countries spanning Europe, Asia, the Americas, and Oceania. It pairs public education spending with three outcome dimensions — academic performance, tertiary access, and youth labor market integration — to enable cross-country comparison.

## Data Source

### education_spending
One row per country. Fields: `country` (string, country name), `region` (string, broad geographic grouping), `edu_spending_pct_gdp` (float, public education expenditure as % of GDP, range ~2.9–7.2%). Based on OECD/World Bank estimates circa 2022.

### pisa_scores
One row per country. Fields: `country` (string), `pisa_avg` (integer, average of reading, math, and science scores from PISA 2022, range 379–561).

### tertiary_enrollment
One row per country. Fields: `country` (string), `enrollment_rate` (integer, gross tertiary enrollment as % of the relevant age cohort, range 43–110%). Values above 100% are possible due to mature-age and international students.

### youth_unemployment
One row per country. Fields: `country` (string), `youth_unemp_rate` (float, unemployment rate for ages 15–24 as % of youth labor force, range ~4.1–30.2%). Data circa 2022–2023.

## Data Notes
- All four datasets share the same 30 countries and are joinable on the `country` field.
- Gross enrollment rates can exceed 100% due to inclusion of students outside the typical age cohort.
- PISA scores represent a combined average; individual subject scores may differ.
- Youth unemployment definitions follow ILO standards but national measurement practices may vary slightly.

import pandas as pd

from scipy.interpolate import UnivariateSpline

unemp = pd.DataFrame(raw['youth_unemployment']['data'])

    'axes.labelcolor': '#222222',
    'xtick.color': '#333333',
    'ytick.color': '#333333',
    'text.color': '#1f1f1f',
    'axes.titlesize': 22,
    'axes.titleweight': 'bold',
    'axes.labelsize': 13,
    'xtick.labelsize': 11,
    'ytick.labelsize': 11,
    'legend.fontsize': 10,
})

fig.subplots_adjust(left=0.09, right=0.88, top=0.84, bottom=0.16)

size_min, size_max = 95, 930
enroll_min, enroll_max = df['enrollment_rate'].min(), df['enrollment_rate'].max()
df['bubble_size'] = np.interp(df['enrollment_rate'], (enroll_min, enroll_max), (size_min, size_max))

# Color encodes youth unemployment; low is blue/green, high is amber/red.
cmap = mpl.colors.LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list(
    'policy_unemployment', ['#2166AC', '#67A9CF', '#F7F7F7', '#FDAE61', '#B2182B']
)
norm = mpl.colors.Normalize(vmin=df['youth_unemp_rate'].min(), vmax=df['youth_unemp_rate'].max())

# Region markers provide extra traceability without competing with the main encodings.
markers = {'Europe': 'o', 'Asia': '^', 'Americas': 's', 'Oceania': 'D'}
for region, group in df.groupby('region'):
    ax.scatter(
        group['edu_spending_pct_gdp'], group['pisa_avg'],
        s=group['bubble_size'], c=group['youth_unemp_rate'],
        cmap=cmap, norm=norm, marker=markers.get(region, 'o'),
        alpha=0.86, edgecolor='#2A2A2A', linewidth=0.85, label=region, zorder=3
    )

# Smooth trend: sorted univariate spline to make the scattered / nonlinear shape visible.
ordered = df.sort_values('edu_spending_pct_gdp')
x = ordered['edu_spending_pct_gdp'].to_numpy()
y = ordered['pisa_avg'].to_numpy()
# Average duplicate x values for a stable spline.
xy = pd.DataFrame({'x': x, 'y': y}).groupby('x', as_index=False)['y'].mean()
xs = np.linspace(xy['x'].min(), xy['x'].max(), 240)
try:
    spline = UnivariateSpline(xy['x'], xy['y'], s=3500)
    ys = spline(xs)
except Exception:
    coef = np.polyfit(x, y, 2)
    ys = np.polyval(coef, xs)
ax.plot(xs, ys, color='#222222', linewidth=2.2, alpha=0.75, zorder=2)
ax.text(6.96, np.interp(6.96, xs, ys) + 8, 'smoothed pattern', fontsize=10, color='#333333', ha='right')

# Reference lines: medians guide interpretation without implying targets.
x_med = df['edu_spending_pct_gdp'].median()
y_med = df['pisa_avg'].median()
ax.axvline(x_med, color='#8A8A8A', linestyle=(0, (4, 4)), linewidth=1.0, alpha=0.7, zorder=1)
ax.axhline(y_med, color='#8A8A8A', linestyle=(0, (4, 4)), linewidth=1.0, alpha=0.7, zorder=1)
ax.text(x_med + 0.03, 563, f'median spending: {x_med:.1f}% GDP', fontsize=9, color='#555555', rotation=90, va='top')
ax.text(2.75, y_med + 2, f'median PISA: {y_med:.0f}', fontsize=9, color='#555555', va='bottom')

# Highlight policy-relevant outliers and mixed-results high spenders.

    'Singapore': (0.12, 8, 'efficiency outlier'),
    'Japan': (0.12, 5, 'efficiency outlier'),
    'South Korea': (0.10, 8, 'high outcomes, moderate spend'),
    'Ireland': (-0.18, 10, 'moderate spend, strong results'),
    'Sweden': (-0.30, 11, 'high spend, high youth unemployment'),
    'Costa Rica': (-0.45, -19, 'high spend, weak outcomes'),
    'Brazil': (0.10, -18, 'high spend, low PISA'),
    'Spain': (0.10, -21, 'enrollment high, jobs weak'),
    'Greece': (0.10, -17, 'enrollment high, jobs weak'),
    'Finland': (0.10, 9, 'high PISA, job-market strain'),
}

for country, (dx, dy, note) in notable.items():
    row = df.loc[df['country'] == country].iloc[0]
    color = '#111111' if country in ['Singapore', 'Japan', 'South Korea', 'Ireland'] else '#5A1E1E'
    ax.annotate(
        country,
        xy=(row['edu_spending_pct_gdp'], row['pisa_avg']),
        xytext=(row['edu_spending_pct_gdp'] + dx, row['pisa_avg'] + dy),
        textcoords='data', fontsize=10.2, fontweight='bold', color=color,
        arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle='-', color=color, lw=0.8, alpha=0.75, shrinkA=2, shrinkB=4),
        zorder=5
    )

# Subtle labels for other high-interest points where space allows.
secondary_labels = ['Estonia', 'Canada', 'United States', 'Mexico', 'Turkey', 'Italy']
secondary_offsets = {
    'Estonia': (0.08, 7), 'Canada': (0.08, 5), 'United States': (0.07, -14),
    'Mexico': (0.08, -12), 'Turkey': (0.08, 8), 'Italy': (0.08, -15)
}
for country in secondary_labels:
    row = df.loc[df['country'] == country].iloc[0]
    dx, dy = secondary_offsets[country]
    ax.text(row['edu_spending_pct_gdp'] + dx, row['pisa_avg'] + dy, country,
            fontsize=8.7, color='#444444', zorder=4)

# Axes and grid
ax.set_xlim(2.6, 7.45)
ax.set_ylim(360, 575)
ax.set_xlabel('Public education spending (% of GDP)')
ax.set_ylabel('PISA performance (average reading, math & science score)')
ax.xaxis.set_major_formatter(mpl.ticker.PercentFormatter(xmax=100, decimals=1))
ax.yaxis.set_major_locator(mpl.ticker.MultipleLocator(25))
ax.grid(True, which='major', color='#D7D2C6', linewidth=0.9, alpha=0.9)
ax.grid(True, which='minor', color='#E9E4DA', linewidth=0.55, alpha=0.8)
ax.minorticks_on()
for spine in ['top', 'right']:
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
ax.spines['left'].set_color('#555555')
ax.spines['bottom'].set_color('#555555')

# Title and subtitle
fig.text(0.09, 0.935, 'Education spending does not map cleanly to outcomes',
         fontsize=22, fontweight='bold', ha='left', va='top', color='#171717')
fig.text(0.09, 0.895,
         '30-country comparison: PISA achievement, tertiary access, and youth unemployment reveal scattered returns and policy outliers',
         fontsize=12.5, ha='left', va='top', color='#454545')

# Colorbar for unemployment
cax = fig.add_axes([0.902, 0.27, 0.018, 0.43])
sm = mpl.cm.ScalarMappable(norm=norm, cmap=cmap)
sm.set_array([])
cbar = fig.colorbar(sm, cax=cax)
cbar.set_label('Youth unemployment\n(% of labor force ages 15–24)', fontsize=10, labelpad=10)
cbar.ax.tick_params(labelsize=9)
cbar.outline.set_edgecolor('#666666')

# Bubble size legend
legend_vals = [55, 80, 110]
legend_handles = [
    plt.scatter([], [], s=np.interp(v, (enroll_min, enroll_max), (size_min, size_max)),
                facecolor='#E3E0D8', edgecolor='#2A2A2A', linewidth=0.8)
    for v in legend_vals
]
size_legend = ax.legend(
    legend_handles, [f'{v}%' for v in legend_vals],
    title='Tertiary enrollment\n(% of age cohort)',
    loc='upper left', bbox_to_anchor=(0.012, 0.982), frameon=True,
    facecolor='#F7F5EF', edgecolor='#BDB6A6', labelspacing=1.2, borderpad=0.9
)
size_legend.get_title().set_fontsize(10)
ax.add_artist(size_legend)

# Region marker legend
region_handles = [Line2D([0], [0], marker=markers[r], color='none', markerfacecolor='#C8C3B8',
                         markeredgecolor='#333333', markersize=8, label=r) for r in ['Europe', 'Asia', 'Americas', 'Oceania']]
reg_legend = ax.legend(
    handles=region_handles, title='Region marker', loc='lower right',

)
reg_legend.get_title().set_fontsize(10)

# In-chart explanatory callouts.
ax.text(2.83, 548,
        'Efficient systems\nlow-to-moderate spend\nwith high PISA and\nlow youth unemployment',
        fontsize=10.5, color='#123C5A', ha='left', va='top',
        bbox=dict(boxstyle='round,pad=0.45', facecolor='#EAF2F7', edgecolor='#8FB5CC', alpha=0.95))
ax.text(6.08, 435,
        'High spenders diverge:\nlarge budgets coexist\nwith weak PISA or difficult\nyouth labor markets',

# Footnote/source
